SKILL.md 35208 .claude/skills/house-style/SKILL.md --- name: house-style description: The house frontend conventions for this repo, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs. Read before writing or editing any component. Covers BEM markup with Tailwind applied in the component stylesheet, the three-file component, the layout grammar (grid for regions, flex for inline runs, no nested flex faking a grid) and the no-raw-literals rule for hand-written CSS. Where these rules and the spartan docs' examples disagree about where utility classes go, these rules win. --- # House frontend conventions These are this repo's conventions, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs (the `spartan` skill). They extend the spartan docs where spartan is silent; they never contradict them. Where spartan already has a rule (semantic colors, `class` is for layout only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, `size-*` for equal dimensions), follow the spartan skill; this file adds only what spartan does not cover. One deliberate exception: spartan's examples put Tailwind utilities in the template's `class` attribute. In this repo they never go there; see "Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet" below. Every other spartan rule stands, including "class is for layout only" on a primitive, which now means the utilities a primitive's BEM class applies must be layout only. ## Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet A template says what things are; the stylesheet says how they look. Utility classes in markup turn every template into a wall of `flex items-center gap-3 sm:w-48` that a reader has to decode to find the structure, and they let styling decisions spread across every file that renders the element. So: 1. **Template classes are BEM names only.** Every token in a `class` attribute, every `[class.x]` binding, and every string inside a `[class]` binding is `block`, `block__element`, `block--modifier` or `block__element--modifier`, lowercase kebab-case. No Tailwind utility appears in a template. That includes `sr-only`: write `class="roster__label"` and `@apply sr-only` it. 2. **One block per component, named after the component file.** `hero-card.ts` owns `.hero-card`, `.hero-card__name`, `.hero-card--retired`, and nothing else. A template must not use another component's block, and a stylesheet must not define one. `:host` is allowed. 3. **Every component is three files.** `hero-card.ts` with `templateUrl: './hero-card.html'` and `styleUrl: './hero-card.css'`. Never `template:` or `styles:`, however small the component. `ng g component` already produces this shape. 4. **Stylesheets are plain `.css` with every BEM class written out in full.** Not `.scss`: Tailwind v4 does not support running behind Sass. The first line is always `@reference "../../styles.css";` (adjust the `../` count to the file's depth under `src/app`), which lets `@apply` resolve the theme's tokens and variants. Write `.roster__row { ... }`, never `.roster { &__row { ... } }`: that is Sass syntax, and native CSS compiles it to a selector that matches nothing, with only a warning. Nesting is fine for states and breakpoints on the same element: `&:hover`, `&::before`, `&[aria-expanded="true"]`, `@media`. 5. **App stylesheets are layout only.** Every utility in `@apply` and every plain declaration in a stylesheet under `src/app`, and every class rule in `src/styles.css`, must be layout: display, flex and grid arrangement, gap, sizing, margin, position, overflow and text alignment (the full list is under "The layout list" below). Color, typography, border, radius, shadow, ring, opacity, transitions, cursor, custom properties and anything not on the list are appearance, and appearance lives in `libs/ui`. Padding is allowed in one place: the component's block root (`.roster`, `.roster--compact`, or `:host`), for the region's inset, and only when that element is not a primitive. Semantic tokens only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, grid for regions. Moving appearance onto a wrapper element, or removing a primitive's directive to keep its look, does not make it allowed. 6. **No utility classes in TypeScript.** No `cva` variant strings, no `host: { class: '...' }`, no computed class strings. A state that changes appearance is a BEM modifier bound with `[class.block--modifier]`. Never build a class name from data (`roster__row--{{ hero.status }}`): write one modifier per state and bind each with `[class.roster__row--active]`, so every class a template can carry is written out in full. Helm directives and their inputs are not classes and stay in the template: `variant`, `size` and the directive itself are the primitive's API. ```html

The shell and theme are in place. `ng build` compiles, and the gates I could run pass.

**Verification**
- `npm run build` compiles. The one warning is the initial bundle budget: 565 kB against a 500 kB budget. It's a warning, not an error, and I didn't try to shrink the bundle.
- `npm run lint`: clean.
- `npm run check:contrast`: all 28 token pairs clear their floors in both themes.
- `npm run check:boot`: all 7 routes render with no runtime errors.
- `npm run check:responsive`: passes at 375, 768 and 1280.
- `npm run check:interaction`: passes, but it found 0 overlays, so it never opened the mobile drawer.
- `npm test`: 2/2 pass.
- `npm run check:wiring` can't run: its script points at `harness/counter/check-wiring.mjs`, which isn't in the tree.

I did not start a dev server.

**What's built**
- **Palette** (`src/styles.css`): the spec's roles are mapped onto spartan's tokens, with the full `--sidebar*` set kept. The rail is dark in both themes.
- **Shell** (`app.ts`, `app.html`, `app.css`): `hlm-sidebar` with its header, nav group, six menu links and footer. `main` is `hlmSidebarInset`. The sidebar's own mobile sheet handles the off-canvas drawer, and a closed drawer isn't rendered at all.
- **Top bar** (`src/app/ui/top-bar/`): a presentational component with inputs and outputs only. It holds the sidebar trigger, breadcrumb, search, notifications button, theme toggle and avatar. Its block root carries the padding.
- **Theme** (`app-shell.view-model.ts`): a component-scoped ViewModel toggles `.dark` on `<html>` and persists the choice under `hero-ops-theme`. With no stored choice it follows `prefers-color-scheme` and tracks changes. `index.html` has a small inline script that applies the theme before first paint.
- **Routes** (`app.routes.ts`): all seven destinations are lazy. Missions, threats, recruit and settings are minimal placeholders. The roster is now at `/roster`, and `/heroes` redirects to it. Unknown URLs redirect to the dashboard.

**Deviations from the spec**
- **On-primary** is `#241a05` (dark ink) in light mode, not `#ffffff`. White on `#d8891a` measures 2.80:1, which fails AA.
- **Focus ring** is a solid `#b26a0c` in light mode, not amber at 35%. The gate reads only six-digit hex and cannot check alpha, and the translucent amber measures about 2.6:1 on the page background.
- **Destructive and info foregrounds** are dark ink, for the same contrast reason.
- **`--sidebar-muted`** is an extra token the spec lists but spartan doesn't have. I defined it and nothing uses it yet, since the rail's text colours come from the primitives.

**Open points**
- **Search** is an uncontrolled input. It doesn't filter or navigate anywhere yet.
- **Roster highlight:** the Roster link isn't highlighted on the hero detail route.
- **Mobile drawer:** nothing has opened it in a browser, so the open-drawer behaviour is unverified.
